clinical: Myocardial infarction territories and coronary dominance

Each coronary branch supplies a predictable territory, so the leads with ST elevation point to the culprit. Anterior interventricular artery (LAD): anterior wall, apex and the anterior two-thirds of the septum, leads V1-V4; an occlusion before the first septal perforator can also injure the bundle branches. Circumflex and its obtuse marginal branches: lateral wall, leads I, aVL, V5-V6 (an isolated circumflex occlusion is often quiet on the ECG). Right coronary artery: about 70-80% of hearts are right-dominant, as this model is, so the RCA supplies the inferior wall through the posterior interventricular artery (leads II, III, aVF) and the posterior wall through the posterolateral branches (ST depression in V1-V3), plus the right ventricle (ST elevation in V4R, hypotension that worsens with nitrates) and usually the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodal arteries, hence bradycardia and heart block. About 10% of hearts are left-dominant: the circumflex then reaches the crux and an inferior infarct is a circumflex event.

Valves are heard downstream of where they lie: aortic, right 2nd intercostal space at the sternal edge; pulmonary, left 2nd space; tricuspid, left lower sternal border; mitral, the apex (left 5th space, midclavicular line). S1 is closure of the atrioventricular valves, S2 of the semilunar valves (A2 then P2, splitting more on inspiration). Aortic stenosis: ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids (calcific degeneration, or a congenitally bicuspid valve). Mitral regurgitation: pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla. Mitral stenosis (rheumatic, with fused commissures and shortened chordae): mid-diastolic rumble with an opening snap, left atrial enlargement and atrial fibrillation. Aortic regurgitation: early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge with a collapsing pulse. Tricuspid regurgitation: pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, louder on inspiration, with large v waves in the jugular pulse, usually from a dilated right ventricle stretching the annulus.
Papillary muscles, chordae and mitral regurgitation

Papillary muscles do not open or close a valve; they tether the leaflets through the chordae so the leaflets are not blown back into the atrium when the ventricle contracts. The anterolateral papillary muscle has a double blood supply (diagonal branches of the LAD and obtuse marginal branches of the circumflex); the posteromedial muscle has a single one (the posterior interventricular artery, from the RCA in right-dominant hearts), so it is the one that ruptures, 2-7 days after an inferior infarct, causing acute severe mitral regurgitation with pulmonary oedema and shock. Ruptured chordae also occur in myxomatous mitral valve prolapse (mid-systolic click, late systolic murmur) and infective endocarditis. A dilated ventricle pulls the papillary muscles apart and tethers the leaflets, giving functional mitral regurgitation.
Atrial fibrillation, the left auricle and the pulmonary veins

Most triggers of atrial fibrillation fire from muscle sleeves that extend into the pulmonary veins, so catheter ablation isolates the four pulmonary vein openings in the back wall of the left atrium. In non-valvular atrial fibrillation about 90% of left atrial thrombi form in the left auricle, a narrow pouch whose blood stagnates; embolism to the brain causes stroke, which is why patients are anticoagulated or the auricle is occluded. The circumflex artery and great cardiac vein run beside the base of the auricle, and the oesophagus lies directly behind the left atrium's posterior wall (atrio-oesophageal fistula is a rare, lethal complication of ablation).
Cardiac veins and the coronary sinus in practice

Most cardiac venous blood returns through the great, middle and small cardiac veins to the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium beside the inferior vena cava; the anterior cardiac veins drain directly into the atrium. Left ventricular leads for cardiac resynchronisation therapy are passed through the coronary sinus opening (which may be guarded by a Thebesian valve) into a lateral or posterior tributary, such as the left marginal vein or the posterior vein of the left ventricle. Retrograde cardioplegia is delivered by a balloon catheter in the coronary sinus. A dilated coronary sinus points to raised right atrial pressure or a persistent left superior vena cava, which drains into it; the oblique vein of the left atrium is that vessel's remnant.

The interatrial septum carries the fossa ovalis, the remnant of the foramen ovale. A patent foramen ovale persists in about a quarter of adults and can let a venous clot cross to the systemic circulation (paradoxical embolism). Atrial septal defects (secundum, in the fossa ovalis, is the commonest) load the right heart and give a fixed split S2. Most ventricular septal defects lie in the small membranous part of the interventricular septum below the aortic valve, beside the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve, and give a harsh pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border; a large left-to-right shunt can reverse as pulmonary vascular resistance rises (Eisenmenger syndrome).

S01.name: Left ventricle
S01.description: The chamber that pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta against systemic pressure, so its wall is roughly three times as thick as the right ventricle's. Here it is five panels, the septum, anterior, lateral and inferior walls and the apex, which are modelling divisions of one muscular wall; hide any of them to see the mitral valve and its papillary muscles from inside.

S02.name: Right ventricle
S02.description: The crescent-shaped chamber that wraps the front of the heart and pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs at low pressure, so its wall is thin. Its inflow part carries the tricuspid valve and papillary muscles; its smooth-walled outflow tract leads to the pulmonary valve. Trabeculae carneae and the moderator band are left out of the model.

S03.name: Left atrium
S03.description: The most posterior chamber. It receives oxygenated blood from the four pulmonary veins through its posterior wall and empties through the mitral valve, and its ear-shaped auricle curls forward on the left. Here it is four panels: anterior wall, posterior wall, interatrial septum and left auricle.

S04.name: Right atrium
S04.description: Receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae and the coronary sinus, and empties through the tricuspid valve. The sinoatrial node, the heart's pacemaker, lies in its wall at the junction with the superior vena cava (not modelled). Here it is three panels: lateral wall, posterior wall and right auricle.

S08.name: Coronary arteries
S08.description: The heart's own arterial supply: the left and right coronary arteries arise from the aortic sinuses just above the aortic valve and run in the fat of the atrioventricular and interventricular grooves, sending branches into the muscle. The model is right-dominant and shows 19 arteries, from the left main trunk to the septal perforators and the nodal arteries. Because the left ventricle squeezes its own vessels shut in systole, most left coronary flow happens in diastole.

S09.name: Cardiac veins
S09.description: Twenty veins that drain the heart wall. The great, middle and small cardiac veins, the posterior vein of the left ventricle and the oblique vein of the left atrium empty into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium; the anterior cardiac veins cross the right ventricle and open into the atrium directly. Most run beside the coronary arteries.

S10.name: Aorta and arch branches
S10.description: The ascending aorta rises from the aortic valve, arches to the left over the pulmonary artery and continues as the descending aorta; the brachiocephalic trunk and the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries leave the arch and are cut short here. Its wall is an elastic artery that stores energy in systole and recoils in diastole.

S11.name: Pulmonary trunk and arteries
S11.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle, runs up and back on the left of the ascending aorta and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries, which carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs (drawn blue, like the veins). The two arteries are cut short at the lung roots.

S12.name: Venae cavae and brachiocephalic veins
S12.description: The right and left brachiocephalic veins unite to form the superior vena cava, which brings blood from the head, neck and arms into the top of the right atrium; the short intrathoracic stub of the inferior vena cava enters from below. All are cut short.

S13.name: Pulmonary veins
S13.description: Two on each side, superior and inferior, they bring oxygenated blood from the lungs into the back of the left atrium (drawn red, unlike the other veins). The right-hand veins pass behind the right atrium and superior vena cava.

S15.name: Tricuspid valve
S15.description: The right atrioventricular valve: three leaflets (anterior, posterior or inferior, and septal) that prevent blood returning from the right ventricle to the right atrium. Each leaflet is held by chordae from the papillary muscles.

S17.name: Mitral valve
S17.description: The left atrioventricular (bicuspid) valve: an anterior and a posterior leaflet that prevent blood returning from the left ventricle to the left atrium. The anterior leaflet is continuous with the aortic valve; both are held by chordae from two papillary muscles.

S20.name: Aortic valve
S20.description: The semilunar valve at the aortic root, with three cusps (left coronary, right coronary and non-coronary); the coronary arteries arise from the sinuses behind the left and right cusps. It closes at the end of ventricular ejection and produces the aortic part of the second heart sound.

S21.name: Pulmonary valve
S21.description: The semilunar valve at the top of the right ventricular outflow tract, with three cusps (anterior, left and right). It is the highest and most anterior of the four valves; no arteries arise from its sinuses.

S22.name: Chordae tendineae
S22.description: Thin tendinous cords that join the leaflets of the atrioventricular valves to the papillary muscles and stop the leaflets prolapsing into the atrium in systole. The model draws six from each of the five papillary muscles (30 in all); in each set the first three run to one leaflet and the last three to the neighbouring leaflet, as each muscle supports the two halves of a commissure.

S23.name: Papillary muscles
S23.description: Conical muscles that project from the ventricular wall and contract with it to keep tension on the chordae. There are two in the left ventricle (anterolateral and posteromedial) and three in the right (anterior, posterior and septal).

S24.name: Valve annuli (fibrous rings)
S24.description: The fibrous rings around the mitral and tricuspid orifices, which anchor the leaflets and separate the atrial from the ventricular muscle. They are part of the fibrous skeleton of the heart, which also includes the aortic and pulmonary rings and the fibrous trigones (not modelled); the atrioventricular bundle is the only normal electrical bridge through it.

interventricular_septum.name: Interventricular septum
interventricular_septum.description: The thick muscular wall between the ventricles; it bulges into the right ventricle and works with the left ventricle. Its anterior two-thirds is supplied by septal perforators of the LAD and its posterior third by the posterior interventricular artery; a small thin membranous part lies just below the aortic valve.

left_ventricle_anterior_wall.name: Left ventricle, anterior wall
left_ventricle_anterior_wall.description: The front wall of the left ventricle, supplied by the LAD and its diagonal branches. Hide it, with the left atrium's anterior wall, to open the outflow tract to the aorta.

left_ventricle_apex.name: Apex of left ventricle
left_ventricle_apex.description: The blunt tip of the heart, formed by the left ventricle and pointing down, forward and to the left; in life it is felt as the apex beat in the left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line. The anterior interventricular artery (LAD) runs down to it.

left_ventricle_inferior_wall.name: Left ventricle, inferior wall
left_ventricle_inferior_wall.description: The diaphragmatic wall on which the heart rests, supplied by the posterior interventricular artery (from the right coronary artery in a right-dominant heart); this is the territory of an inferior infarct.

left_ventricle_lateral_wall.name: Left ventricle, lateral wall
left_ventricle_lateral_wall.description: The free left wall, supplied by the obtuse marginal branches of the circumflex artery. Hide it to see the two mitral papillary muscles and their chordae.

right_ventricle_anterior_wall.name: Right ventricle, anterior wall
right_ventricle_anterior_wall.description: The sternocostal wall of the right ventricle, supplied by right ventricular branches of the right coronary artery and small branches of the LAD. Hide it to see the tricuspid valve and its anterior papillary muscle.

right_ventricle_inferior_wall.name: Right ventricle, inferior wall
right_ventricle_inferior_wall.description: The diaphragmatic wall of the right ventricle, running to the acute margin and supplied by the right coronary artery.

right_ventricle_outflow_tract.name: Right ventricle, outflow tract (conus arteriosus)
right_ventricle_outflow_tract.description: The smooth-walled funnel, also called the infundibulum, that leads from the ventricle to the pulmonary valve. The conus artery runs across it; hide it to look into the funnel below the valve.

interatrial_septum.name: Interatrial septum
interatrial_septum.description: The thin wall between the two atria. On its right-atrial face lies the fossa ovalis, the remnant of the fetal foramen ovale; viewed from the left, it is exposed by hiding the posterior wall of the left atrium.

left_atrium_anterior_wall.name: Left atrium, anterior wall
left_atrium_anterior_wall.description: The wall that faces forward and lies directly behind the aortic root; the root's bulge into it is real anatomy, not a fault.

left_atrium_posterior_wall.name: Left atrium, posterior wall
left_atrium_posterior_wall.description: The smooth back wall that receives the four pulmonary veins. It lies just in front of the oesophagus, which an enlarged left atrium can compress.

left_auricle.name: Left auricle (left atrial appendage)
left_auricle.description: The narrow, hook-shaped pouch of the left atrium that curls forward beside the pulmonary trunk. Blood stagnates in it in atrial fibrillation, making it the main site of atrial thrombi. The circumflex artery and great cardiac vein run beneath its base.

right_atrium_lateral_wall.name: Right atrium, lateral wall
right_atrium_lateral_wall.description: The free right wall of the atrium. In life its inner surface is ridged by the pectinate muscles running from the crista terminalis (not modelled); the right coronary artery runs in the groove at its lower edge.

right_atrium_posterior_wall.name: Right atrium, posterior wall
right_atrium_posterior_wall.description: The smooth-walled part of the atrium that receives the superior and inferior venae cavae, with the coronary sinus opening between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid ring.

right_auricle.name: Right auricle (right atrial appendage)
right_auricle.description: The broad triangular pouch that overlaps the root of the aorta on the right. The right coronary artery lies in the groove below it and the sinoatrial nodal artery passes beside its base.

left_main_coronary_artery.name: Left coronary artery (left main)
left_main_coronary_artery.description: Arises from the aorta above the left coronary cusp and passes behind the pulmonary trunk, about 1-2.5 cm long, before dividing into the anterior interventricular artery and the circumflex artery. Together its branches supply most of the left ventricle and the septum.

left_anterior_descending_artery.name: Anterior interventricular artery (LAD)
left_anterior_descending_artery.description: The left anterior descending artery runs in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex, giving the diagonal and septal perforator branches. It supplies the anterior left ventricular wall, the apex and the anterior two-thirds of the septum.

left_circumflex_artery.name: Circumflex artery (LCx)
left_circumflex_artery.description: Runs to the left in the atrioventricular groove beneath the left auricle, giving the obtuse marginal branches and ending in a posterolateral branch. It supplies the lateral and posterolateral left ventricle and, in about 40% of hearts, the sinoatrial node.

first_diagonal_artery.name: First diagonal artery
first_diagonal_artery.description: The first and usually largest diagonal, leaving the LAD near its origin and running over the anterolateral left ventricular wall, which it supplies together with the anterolateral papillary muscle.

second_diagonal_artery.name: Second diagonal artery
second_diagonal_artery.description: A diagonal branch of the LAD supplying the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle.

third_diagonal_artery.name: Third diagonal artery
third_diagonal_artery.description: The most distal of the three diagonal branches of the LAD, supplying the lower anterolateral wall.

first_septal_perforator.name: First septal perforator
first_septal_perforator.description: The most proximal septal branch of the LAD. It dives into the upper septum and often supplies the proximal conduction system; it is the target of alcohol septal ablation in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
atlas: Septal branches of anterior interventricular artery

second_septal_perforator.name: Second septal perforator
second_septal_perforator.description: A septal branch of the LAD passing into the middle of the interventricular septum; septal perforators anastomose with septal branches of the posterior interventricular artery.
atlas: Septal branches of anterior interventricular artery

third_septal_perforator.name: Third septal perforator
third_septal_perforator.description: A distal septal branch of the LAD supplying the lower septum.
atlas: Septal branches of anterior interventricular artery

first_obtuse_marginal_artery.name: First obtuse marginal artery
first_obtuse_marginal_artery.description: The first marginal branch of the circumflex artery (the left marginal artery), running down the rounded left border of the heart to supply the lateral wall of the left ventricle.

second_obtuse_marginal_artery.name: Second obtuse marginal artery
second_obtuse_marginal_artery.description: The second marginal branch of the circumflex artery, supplying the lower lateral wall of the left ventricle.

posterolateral_branch_of_circumflex.name: Posterolateral branch of circumflex artery
posterolateral_branch_of_circumflex.description: The terminal branch of the circumflex artery, supplying the posterolateral wall of the left ventricle.

right_coronary_artery.name: Right coronary artery
right_coronary_artery.description: Arises from the aorta above the right coronary cusp and runs in the right atrioventricular groove around the acute margin to the crux. It supplies the right atrium, most of the right ventricle, the inferior wall of the left ventricle and, in most people, the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes.

conus_artery.name: Conus artery (conus arteriosus branch)
conus_artery.description: The first branch of the right coronary artery in this model (in many hearts it has its own opening in the aorta). It runs across the right ventricular outflow tract towards the LAD, forming a possible collateral link between the two coronary arteries.

sinoatrial_nodal_artery.name: Sinoatrial (SA) nodal artery
sinoatrial_nodal_artery.description: Arises from the proximal right coronary artery (as in about 60% of hearts; in the rest from the circumflex), runs up over the right auricle beside the aorta and on to the junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrium, where the sinoatrial node lies.

right_marginal_artery.name: Right marginal artery
right_marginal_artery.description: The acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery, running along the sharp lower border of the heart to supply the free wall of the right ventricle.

posterior_descending_artery.name: Posterior interventricular artery
posterior_descending_artery.description: The posterior descending artery (PDA) runs in the posterior interventricular groove towards the apex. In this right-dominant heart it comes from the right coronary artery at the crux and supplies the posterior third of the septum, the inferior wall and the posteromedial papillary muscle.

right_posterolateral_artery.name: Right posterolateral artery
right_posterolateral_artery.description: The continuation of the right coronary artery beyond the crux onto the posterior wall of the left ventricle, present in right-dominant hearts.
atlas: Right inferolateral branch of right coronary artery

atrioventricular_nodal_artery.name: Atrioventricular (AV) nodal artery
atrioventricular_nodal_artery.description: A small branch that arises at the crux, from the right coronary artery in about 80-90% of hearts, and runs to the atrioventricular node, so an inferior infarct often causes heart block.

coronary_sinus.name: Coronary sinus
coronary_sinus.description: The largest cardiac vein, lying in the posterior atrioventricular groove. It receives the great, middle and small cardiac veins, the posterior vein of the left ventricle and the oblique vein of the left atrium, and opens into the right atrium between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid orifice.

great_cardiac_vein.name: Great cardiac vein
great_cardiac_vein.description: Begins near the apex, climbs the anterior interventricular groove beside the LAD, then curves left beside the circumflex artery in the atrioventricular groove and becomes the coronary sinus where the oblique vein of the left atrium joins. It drains the anterior left ventricle and septum.

great_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.name: Great cardiac vein, tributary 1
great_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.description: The most apical of four short tributaries that drain the anterior and anterolateral left ventricular wall into the great cardiac vein.

great_cardiac_vein_tributary_2.name: Great cardiac vein, tributary 2
great_cardiac_vein_tributary_2.description: The second tributary of the great cardiac vein, counting from the apex.

great_cardiac_vein_tributary_3.name: Great cardiac vein, tributary 3
great_cardiac_vein_tributary_3.description: The third tributary of the great cardiac vein, counting from the apex.

great_cardiac_vein_tributary_4.name: Great cardiac vein, tributary 4
great_cardiac_vein_tributary_4.description: The most basal tributary of the great cardiac vein, entering near the origin of the circumflex artery.

left_marginal_vein.name: Left marginal vein
left_marginal_vein.description: Ascends the rounded left border of the heart beside the obtuse marginal artery and drains into the great cardiac vein. It is a common target vein for a left ventricular pacing lead.

left_marginal_vein_tributary_1.name: Left marginal vein, tributary 1
left_marginal_vein_tributary_1.description: A small tributary joining the left marginal vein from the lateral wall.

left_marginal_vein_tributary_2.name: Left marginal vein, tributary 2
left_marginal_vein_tributary_2.description: A small tributary joining the left marginal vein from the posterolateral wall.

middle_cardiac_vein.name: Middle cardiac vein
middle_cardiac_vein.description: Starts near the apex, runs up the posterior interventricular groove beside the posterior interventricular artery and ends in the coronary sinus close to its opening. It drains the posterior parts of both ventricles and of the septum.

middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.name: Middle cardiac vein, tributary 1
middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.description: A small apical tributary of the middle cardiac vein.

middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_2.name: Middle cardiac vein, tributary 2
middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_2.description: A small tributary of the middle cardiac vein from the inferior wall near the apex.

middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_3.name: Middle cardiac vein, tributary 3
middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_3.description: A tributary that links the middle cardiac vein with the posterior vein of the left ventricle.

small_cardiac_vein.name: Small cardiac vein
small_cardiac_vein.description: Runs in the right atrioventricular groove beside the right coronary artery and its marginal branch, draining the right atrium and right ventricle into the coronary sinus near its opening.

small_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.name: Small cardiac vein, tributary 1
small_cardiac_vein_tributary_1.description: A small tributary from the inferior wall of the right ventricle joining the small cardiac vein.

posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle
posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle.description: Runs on the inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle, parallel to the middle cardiac vein, and enters the coronary sinus. Called the inferior vein of the left ventricle in current terminology.

posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle_tributa.name: Posterior vein of left ventricle, tributary 1
posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle_tributa.description: A small tributary of the posterior vein of the left ventricle.

oblique_vein_of_left_atrium.name: Oblique vein of left atrium (of Marshall)
oblique_vein_of_left_atrium.description: A small vein running down the back of the left atrium to the coronary sinus, a remnant of the embryonic left common cardinal vein (which persists as a left superior vena cava in some people). Where it joins marks the start of the coronary sinus.

first_anterior_cardiac_vein.name: First anterior cardiac vein
first_anterior_cardiac_vein.description: One of the small veins on the front of the right ventricle that cross the right atrioventricular groove and open directly into the right atrium, not through the coronary sinus.

second_anterior_cardiac_vein.name: Second anterior cardiac vein
second_anterior_cardiac_vein.description: A second small anterior vein of the right ventricle, draining straight into the right atrium.

ascending_aorta.name: Ascending aorta
ascending_aorta.description: Rises from the aortic root, enclosed in the pericardium with the pulmonary trunk; its first branches are the coronary arteries. It is the usual site of type A aortic dissection.

aortic_arch.name: Aortic arch
aortic_arch.description: Curves back over the left pulmonary artery and left main bronchus, giving off the brachiocephalic trunk, the left common carotid and the left subclavian arteries. The ligamentum arteriosum (not modelled) ties it to the left pulmonary artery.

brachiocephalic_trunk.name: Brachiocephalic trunk
brachiocephalic_trunk.description: The first and largest branch of the arch; it divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries behind the right sternoclavicular joint (cut short here).

left_common_carotid_artery.name: Left common carotid artery
left_common_carotid_artery.description: The second branch of the arch, supplying the left side of the head and neck (cut short here).

left_subclavian_artery.name: Left subclavian artery
left_subclavian_artery.description: The third branch of the arch, supplying the left arm and giving the left vertebral artery (cut short here).

descending_aorta.name: Descending (thoracic) aorta
descending_aorta.description: Continues from the arch at about the level of the sternal angle and runs down the left side of the vertebral column (cut here).

pulmonary_trunk.name: Pulmonary trunk
pulmonary_trunk.description: About 5 cm long, it leaves the right ventricle at the pulmonary valve and runs up and back on the left of the ascending aorta before dividing beneath the aortic arch into the two pulmonary arteries.

right_pulmonary_artery.name: Right pulmonary artery
right_pulmonary_artery.description: The longer branch: it passes behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava, in front of the right main bronchus, to the right lung.

left_pulmonary_artery.name: Left pulmonary artery
left_pulmonary_artery.description: The shorter branch, arching over the left main bronchus to the left lung; the ligamentum arteriosum joins it to the aortic arch.

superior_vena_cava.name: Superior vena cava
superior_vena_cava.description: Formed by the two brachiocephalic veins and about 7 cm long in life, it drains the head, neck and arms into the top of the right atrium. It has no valves, and the sinoatrial node lies at its junction with the atrium.

inferior_vena_cava.name: Inferior vena cava
inferior_vena_cava.description: Only its short intrathoracic part is shown, between the diaphragm and the right atrium, which it enters from below.

right_brachiocephalic_vein.name: Right brachiocephalic vein
right_brachiocephalic_vein.description: The short, almost vertical vein that joins the left brachiocephalic vein to form the superior vena cava.

left_brachiocephalic_vein.name: Left brachiocephalic vein
left_brachiocephalic_vein.description: The longer, oblique vein that crosses in front of the three arch branches to join the right one and form the superior vena cava.

left_superior_pulmonary_vein.name: Left superior pulmonary vein
left_superior_pulmonary_vein.description: Drains the left upper lobe and lingula into the left atrium, opening beside the left auricle.

left_inferior_pulmonary_vein.name: Left inferior pulmonary vein
left_inferior_pulmonary_vein.description: Drains the left lower lobe into the left atrium.

right_superior_pulmonary_vein.name: Right superior pulmonary vein
right_superior_pulmonary_vein.description: Drains the right upper and middle lobes into the left atrium, passing behind the right atrium and superior vena cava.

right_inferior_pulmonary_vein.name: Right inferior pulmonary vein
right_inferior_pulmonary_vein.description: Drains the right lower lobe into the left atrium.

tricuspid_anterior_leaflet.name: Anterior leaflet of tricuspid valve
tricuspid_anterior_leaflet.description: The largest leaflet, lying over the front wall of the right ventricle towards the outflow tract. Its chordae come from the anterior and septal papillary muscles.

tricuspid_posterior_leaflet.name: Posterior (inferior) leaflet of tricuspid valve
tricuspid_posterior_leaflet.description: The smallest leaflet, lying along the inferior wall of the ventricle. Its chordae come from the posterior and anterior papillary muscles.
atlas: Inferior leaflet of right atrioventricular valve

tricuspid_septal_leaflet.name: Septal leaflet of tricuspid valve
tricuspid_septal_leaflet.description: Attached to the interventricular septum, with chordae from the septal and posterior papillary muscles. The atrioventricular node and bundle lie close to its base (the triangle of Koch), so surgery here risks heart block; in Ebstein anomaly it is displaced towards the apex.
atlas: Septal leaflet of right atrioventricular valve

mitral_anterior_leaflet.name: Anterior (aortic) leaflet of mitral valve
mitral_anterior_leaflet.description: The taller, more mobile leaflet: it hangs between the mitral and aortic orifices and is continuous with the aortic valve (between the left and non-coronary cusps), but occupies only about a third of the annulus.

mitral_posterior_leaflet.name: Posterior (mural) leaflet of mitral valve
mitral_posterior_leaflet.description: Attached along about two-thirds of the annulus; in life it has three scallops (P1 to P3) and is the leaflet most often involved in prolapse.
atlas: Posterior leaflet of left atrioventricular valve

aortic_left_coronary_cusp.name: Left coronary cusp of aortic valve
aortic_left_coronary_cusp.description: Faces the opening of the left coronary artery and lies posteriorly on the left; the anterior mitral leaflet is continuous with the valve beneath the junction of this cusp and the non-coronary cusp.

aortic_right_coronary_cusp.name: Right coronary cusp of aortic valve
aortic_right_coronary_cusp.description: The most anterior cusp, facing the opening of the right coronary artery; in most bicuspid aortic valves it is fused with the left coronary cusp.

aortic_non_coronary_cusp.name: Non-coronary cusp of aortic valve
aortic_non_coronary_cusp.description: The posterior cusp, with no coronary artery behind it; it lies next to the interatrial septum and the right atrium.

pulmonary_anterior_cusp.name: Anterior cusp of pulmonary valve
pulmonary_anterior_cusp.description: The anterior cusp of the pulmonary valve, the most forward valve cusp in the heart.
atlas: Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valve

pulmonary_left_cusp.name: Left cusp of pulmonary valve
pulmonary_left_cusp.description: The cusp on the patient's left side of the pulmonary valve.
atlas: Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valve

pulmonary_right_cusp.name: Right cusp of pulmonary valve
pulmonary_right_cusp.description: The cusp on the patient's right side of the pulmonary valve.
atlas: Right semilunar leaflet of pulmonary valve

mitral_anterolateral_papillary_muscle.name: Anterolateral papillary muscle (mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_papillary_muscle.description: Arises from the lateral wall of the left ventricle. It has a double blood supply (LAD diagonals and circumflex marginals), so it rarely ruptures after an infarct.

mitral_posteromedial_papillary_muscle.name: Posteromedial papillary muscle (mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_papillary_muscle.description: Arises from the inferior part of the left ventricular wall. It usually has a single supply, the posterior interventricular artery, so it is the muscle that ruptures after an inferior infarct.
atlas: Inferior papillary muscle of left ventricle

tricuspid_anterior_papillary_muscle.name: Anterior papillary muscle (tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_papillary_muscle.description: The largest right ventricular papillary muscle, from the anterior wall; in life the moderator band (not modelled) joins it to the septum.
atlas: Anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle

tricuspid_posterior_papillary_muscle.name: Posterior papillary muscle (tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_papillary_muscle.description: Arises from the inferior wall of the right ventricle, often as two or three heads.
atlas: Inferior papillary muscle of right ventricle

tricuspid_septal_papillary_muscle.name: Septal papillary muscle (tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_papillary_muscle.description: The smallest right ventricular papillary muscle, arising from the septum, sometimes rudimentary.
atlas: Septal papillary muscle of right ventricle

mitral_annulus.name: Mitral annulus
mitral_annulus.description: The fibrous ring of the mitral orifice, about 3.2 cm across in this model. It dilates in left atrial and ventricular enlargement (functional mitral regurgitation) and calcifies in the elderly.

tricuspid_annulus.name: Tricuspid annulus
tricuspid_annulus.description: The fibrous ring of the tricuspid orifice, about 3.6 cm across in this model. It stretches when the right ventricle dilates, causing functional tricuspid regurgitation.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_1.name: Chorda tendinea 1 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_1.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_2.name: Chorda tendinea 2 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_2.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_3.name: Chorda tendinea 3 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_3.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_4.name: Chorda tendinea 4 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_4.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_5.name: Chorda tendinea 5 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_5.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_anterolateral_chorda_6.name: Chorda tendinea 6 (anterolateral papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_anterolateral_chorda_6.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_1.name: Chorda tendinea 1 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_1.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_2.name: Chorda tendinea 2 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_2.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_3.name: Chorda tendinea 3 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_3.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_4.name: Chorda tendinea 4 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_4.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_5.name: Chorda tendinea 5 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_5.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

mitral_posteromedial_chorda_6.name: Chorda tendinea 6 (posteromedial papillary muscle, mitral)
mitral_posteromedial_chorda_6.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_1.name: Chorda tendinea 1 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_1.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_2.name: Chorda tendinea 2 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_2.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_3.name: Chorda tendinea 3 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_3.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_4.name: Chorda tendinea 4 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_4.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_5.name: Chorda tendinea 5 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_5.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_anterior_chorda_6.name: Chorda tendinea 6 (anterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_anterior_chorda_6.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_1.name: Chorda tendinea 1 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_1.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_2.name: Chorda tendinea 2 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_2.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_3.name: Chorda tendinea 3 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_3.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_4.name: Chorda tendinea 4 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_4.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_5.name: Chorda tendinea 5 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_5.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_posterior_chorda_6.name: Chorda tendinea 6 (posterior papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_posterior_chorda_6.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_1.name: Chorda tendinea 1 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_1.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_2.name: Chorda tendinea 2 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_2.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_3.name: Chorda tendinea 3 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_3.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_4.name: Chorda tendinea 4 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_4.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_5.name: Chorda tendinea 5 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_5.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

tricuspid_septal_chorda_6.name: Chorda tendinea 6 (septal papillary muscle, tricuspid)
tricuspid_septal_chorda_6.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: interatrial_septum
parts.description: The thin wall between the two atria. On its right-atrial face lies the fossa ovalis, the remnant of the fetal foramen ovale; viewed from the left, it is exposed by hiding the posterior wall of the left atrium.

parts.name: interventricular_septum
parts.description: The thick muscular wall between the ventricles; it bulges into the right ventricle and works with the left ventricle. Its anterior two-thirds is supplied by septal perforators of the LAD and its posterior third by the posterior interventricular artery; a small thin membranous part lies just below the aortic valve.

parts.name: left_atrium_anterior_wall
parts.description: The wall that faces forward and lies directly behind the aortic root; the root's bulge into it is real anatomy, not a fault.

parts.name: left_atrium_posterior_wall
parts.description: The smooth back wall that receives the four pulmonary veins. It lies just in front of the oesophagus, which an enlarged left atrium can compress.

parts.name: left_auricle
parts.description: The narrow, hook-shaped pouch of the left atrium that curls forward beside the pulmonary trunk. Blood stagnates in it in atrial fibrillation, making it the main site of atrial thrombi. The circumflex artery and great cardiac vein run beneath its base.

parts.name: left_ventricle_anterior_wall
parts.description: The front wall of the left ventricle, supplied by the LAD and its diagonal branches. Hide it, with the left atrium's anterior wall, to open the outflow tract to the aorta.

parts.name: left_ventricle_apex
parts.description: The blunt tip of the heart, formed by the left ventricle and pointing down, forward and to the left; in life it is felt as the apex beat in the left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line. The anterior interventricular artery (LAD) runs down to it.

parts.name: left_ventricle_inferior_wall
parts.description: The diaphragmatic wall on which the heart rests, supplied by the posterior interventricular artery (from the right coronary artery in a right-dominant heart); this is the territory of an inferior infarct.

parts.name: left_ventricle_lateral_wall
parts.description: The free left wall, supplied by the obtuse marginal branches of the circumflex artery. Hide it to see the two mitral papillary muscles and their chordae.

parts.name: right_atrium_lateral_wall
parts.description: The free right wall of the atrium. In life its inner surface is ridged by the pectinate muscles running from the crista terminalis (not modelled); the right coronary artery runs in the groove at its lower edge.

parts.name: right_atrium_posterior_wall
parts.description: The smooth-walled part of the atrium that receives the superior and inferior venae cavae, with the coronary sinus opening between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid ring.

parts.name: right_auricle
parts.description: The broad triangular pouch that overlaps the root of the aorta on the right. The right coronary artery lies in the groove below it and the sinoatrial nodal artery passes beside its base.

parts.name: right_ventricle_anterior_wall
parts.description: The sternocostal wall of the right ventricle, supplied by right ventricular branches of the right coronary artery and small branches of the LAD. Hide it to see the tricuspid valve and its anterior papillary muscle.

parts.name: right_ventricle_inferior_wall
parts.description: The diaphragmatic wall of the right ventricle, running to the acute margin and supplied by the right coronary artery.

parts.name: right_ventricle_outflow_tract
parts.description: The smooth-walled funnel, also called the infundibulum, that leads from the ventricle to the pulmonary valve. The conus artery runs across it; hide it to look into the funnel below the valve.

parts.name: atrioventricular_nodal_artery
parts.description: A small branch that arises at the crux, from the right coronary artery in about 80-90% of hearts, and runs to the atrioventricular node, so an inferior infarct often causes heart block.

parts.name: conus_artery
parts.description: The first branch of the right coronary artery in this model (in many hearts it has its own opening in the aorta). It runs across the right ventricular outflow tract towards the LAD, forming a possible collateral link between the two coronary arteries.

parts.name: coronary_sinus
parts.description: The largest cardiac vein, lying in the posterior atrioventricular groove. It receives the great, middle and small cardiac veins, the posterior vein of the left ventricle and the oblique vein of the left atrium, and opens into the right atrium between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid orifice.

parts.name: first_anterior_cardiac_vein
parts.description: One of the small veins on the front of the right ventricle that cross the right atrioventricular groove and open directly into the right atrium, not through the coronary sinus.

parts.name: first_diagonal_artery
parts.description: The first and usually largest diagonal, leaving the LAD near its origin and running over the anterolateral left ventricular wall, which it supplies together with the anterolateral papillary muscle.

parts.name: first_obtuse_marginal_artery
parts.description: The first marginal branch of the circumflex artery (the left marginal artery), running down the rounded left border of the heart to supply the lateral wall of the left ventricle.

parts.name: first_septal_perforator
parts.description: The most proximal septal branch of the LAD. It dives into the upper septum and often supplies the proximal conduction system; it is the target of alcohol septal ablation in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

parts.name: great_cardiac_vein
parts.description: Begins near the apex, climbs the anterior interventricular groove beside the LAD, then curves left beside the circumflex artery in the atrioventricular groove and becomes the coronary sinus where the oblique vein of the left atrium joins. It drains the anterior left ventricle and septum.

parts.name: great_cardiac_vein_tributary_1
parts.description: The most apical of four short tributaries that drain the anterior and anterolateral left ventricular wall into the great cardiac vein.

parts.name: great_cardiac_vein_tributary_2
parts.description: The second tributary of the great cardiac vein, counting from the apex.

parts.name: great_cardiac_vein_tributary_3
parts.description: The third tributary of the great cardiac vein, counting from the apex.

parts.name: great_cardiac_vein_tributary_4
parts.description: The most basal tributary of the great cardiac vein, entering near the origin of the circumflex artery.

parts.name: left_anterior_descending_artery
parts.description: The left anterior descending artery runs in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex, giving the diagonal and septal perforator branches. It supplies the anterior left ventricular wall, the apex and the anterior two-thirds of the septum.

parts.name: left_circumflex_artery
parts.description: Runs to the left in the atrioventricular groove beneath the left auricle, giving the obtuse marginal branches and ending in a posterolateral branch. It supplies the lateral and posterolateral left ventricle and, in about 40% of hearts, the sinoatrial node.

parts.name: left_main_coronary_artery
parts.description: Arises from the aorta above the left coronary cusp and passes behind the pulmonary trunk, about 1-2.5 cm long, before dividing into the anterior interventricular artery and the circumflex artery. Together its branches supply most of the left ventricle and the septum.

parts.name: left_marginal_vein
parts.description: Ascends the rounded left border of the heart beside the obtuse marginal artery and drains into the great cardiac vein. It is a common target vein for a left ventricular pacing lead.

parts.name: left_marginal_vein_tributary_1
parts.description: A small tributary joining the left marginal vein from the lateral wall.

parts.name: left_marginal_vein_tributary_2
parts.description: A small tributary joining the left marginal vein from the posterolateral wall.

parts.name: middle_cardiac_vein
parts.description: Starts near the apex, runs up the posterior interventricular groove beside the posterior interventricular artery and ends in the coronary sinus close to its opening. It drains the posterior parts of both ventricles and of the septum.

parts.name: middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_1
parts.description: A small apical tributary of the middle cardiac vein.

parts.name: middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_2
parts.description: A small tributary of the middle cardiac vein from the inferior wall near the apex.

parts.name: middle_cardiac_vein_tributary_3
parts.description: A tributary that links the middle cardiac vein with the posterior vein of the left ventricle.

parts.name: oblique_vein_of_left_atrium
parts.description: A small vein running down the back of the left atrium to the coronary sinus, a remnant of the embryonic left common cardinal vein (which persists as a left superior vena cava in some people). Where it joins marks the start of the coronary sinus.

parts.name: posterior_descending_artery
parts.description: The posterior descending artery (PDA) runs in the posterior interventricular groove towards the apex. In this right-dominant heart it comes from the right coronary artery at the crux and supplies the posterior third of the septum, the inferior wall and the posteromedial papillary muscle.

parts.name: posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle
parts.description: Runs on the inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle, parallel to the middle cardiac vein, and enters the coronary sinus. Called the inferior vein of the left ventricle in current terminology.

parts.name: posterior_vein_of_left_ventricle_tributary_1
parts.description: A small tributary of the posterior vein of the left ventricle.

parts.name: posterolateral_branch_of_circumflex
parts.description: The terminal branch of the circumflex artery, supplying the posterolateral wall of the left ventricle.

parts.name: right_coronary_artery
parts.description: Arises from the aorta above the right coronary cusp and runs in the right atrioventricular groove around the acute margin to the crux. It supplies the right atrium, most of the right ventricle, the inferior wall of the left ventricle and, in most people, the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes.

parts.name: right_marginal_artery
parts.description: The acute marginal branch of the right coronary artery, running along the sharp lower border of the heart to supply the free wall of the right ventricle.

parts.name: right_posterolateral_artery
parts.description: The continuation of the right coronary artery beyond the crux onto the posterior wall of the left ventricle, present in right-dominant hearts.

parts.name: second_anterior_cardiac_vein
parts.description: A second small anterior vein of the right ventricle, draining straight into the right atrium.

parts.name: second_diagonal_artery
parts.description: A diagonal branch of the LAD supplying the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle.

parts.name: second_obtuse_marginal_artery
parts.description: The second marginal branch of the circumflex artery, supplying the lower lateral wall of the left ventricle.

parts.name: second_septal_perforator
parts.description: A septal branch of the LAD passing into the middle of the interventricular septum; septal perforators anastomose with septal branches of the posterior interventricular artery.

parts.name: sinoatrial_nodal_artery
parts.description: Arises from the proximal right coronary artery (as in about 60% of hearts; in the rest from the circumflex), runs up over the right auricle beside the aorta and on to the junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrium, where the sinoatrial node lies.

parts.name: small_cardiac_vein
parts.description: Runs in the right atrioventricular groove beside the right coronary artery and its marginal branch, draining the right atrium and right ventricle into the coronary sinus near its opening.

parts.name: small_cardiac_vein_tributary_1
parts.description: A small tributary from the inferior wall of the right ventricle joining the small cardiac vein.

parts.name: third_diagonal_artery
parts.description: The most distal of the three diagonal branches of the LAD, supplying the lower anterolateral wall.

parts.name: third_septal_perforator
parts.description: A distal septal branch of the LAD supplying the lower septum.

parts.name: aortic_arch
parts.description: Curves back over the left pulmonary artery and left main bronchus, giving off the brachiocephalic trunk, the left common carotid and the left subclavian arteries. The ligamentum arteriosum (not modelled) ties it to the left pulmonary artery.

parts.name: ascending_aorta
parts.description: Rises from the aortic root, enclosed in the pericardium with the pulmonary trunk; its first branches are the coronary arteries. It is the usual site of type A aortic dissection.

parts.name: brachiocephalic_trunk
parts.description: The first and largest branch of the arch; it divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries behind the right sternoclavicular joint (cut short here).

parts.name: descending_aorta
parts.description: Continues from the arch at about the level of the sternal angle and runs down the left side of the vertebral column (cut here).

parts.name: inferior_vena_cava
parts.description: Only its short intrathoracic part is shown, between the diaphragm and the right atrium, which it enters from below.

parts.name: left_brachiocephalic_vein
parts.description: The longer, oblique vein that crosses in front of the three arch branches to join the right one and form the superior vena cava.

parts.name: left_common_carotid_artery
parts.description: The second branch of the arch, supplying the left side of the head and neck (cut short here).

parts.name: left_inferior_pulmonary_vein
parts.description: Drains the left lower lobe into the left atrium.

parts.name: left_pulmonary_artery
parts.description: The shorter branch, arching over the left main bronchus to the left lung; the ligamentum arteriosum joins it to the aortic arch.

parts.name: left_subclavian_artery
parts.description: The third branch of the arch, supplying the left arm and giving the left vertebral artery (cut short here).

parts.name: left_superior_pulmonary_vein
parts.description: Drains the left upper lobe and lingula into the left atrium, opening beside the left auricle.

parts.name: pulmonary_trunk
parts.description: About 5 cm long, it leaves the right ventricle at the pulmonary valve and runs up and back on the left of the ascending aorta before dividing beneath the aortic arch into the two pulmonary arteries.

parts.name: right_brachiocephalic_vein
parts.description: The short, almost vertical vein that joins the left brachiocephalic vein to form the superior vena cava.

parts.name: right_inferior_pulmonary_vein
parts.description: Drains the right lower lobe into the left atrium.

parts.name: right_pulmonary_artery
parts.description: The longer branch: it passes behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava, in front of the right main bronchus, to the right lung.

parts.name: right_superior_pulmonary_vein
parts.description: Drains the right upper and middle lobes into the left atrium, passing behind the right atrium and superior vena cava.

parts.name: superior_vena_cava
parts.description: Formed by the two brachiocephalic veins and about 7 cm long in life, it drains the head, neck and arms into the top of the right atrium. It has no valves, and the sinoatrial node lies at its junction with the atrium.

parts.name: aortic_left_coronary_cusp
parts.description: Faces the opening of the left coronary artery and lies posteriorly on the left; the anterior mitral leaflet is continuous with the valve beneath the junction of this cusp and the non-coronary cusp.

parts.name: aortic_non_coronary_cusp
parts.description: The posterior cusp, with no coronary artery behind it; it lies next to the interatrial septum and the right atrium.

parts.name: aortic_right_coronary_cusp
parts.description: The most anterior cusp, facing the opening of the right coronary artery; in most bicuspid aortic valves it is fused with the left coronary cusp.

parts.name: mitral_annulus
parts.description: The fibrous ring of the mitral orifice, about 3.2 cm across in this model. It dilates in left atrial and ventricular enlargement (functional mitral regurgitation) and calcifies in the elderly.

parts.name: mitral_anterior_leaflet
parts.description: The taller, more mobile leaflet: it hangs between the mitral and aortic orifices and is continuous with the aortic valve (between the left and non-coronary cusps), but occupies only about a third of the annulus.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_1
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_2
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_3
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_4
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_5
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_chorda_6
parts.description: Runs from the anterolateral papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_anterolateral_papillary_muscle
parts.description: Arises from the lateral wall of the left ventricle. It has a double blood supply (LAD diagonals and circumflex marginals), so it rarely ruptures after an infarct.

parts.name: mitral_posterior_leaflet
parts.description: Attached along about two-thirds of the annulus; in life it has three scallops (P1 to P3) and is the leaflet most often involved in prolapse.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_1
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_2
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_3
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_4
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_5
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_chorda_6
parts.description: Runs from the posteromedial papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve.

parts.name: mitral_posteromedial_papillary_muscle
parts.description: Arises from the inferior part of the left ventricular wall. It usually has a single supply, the posterior interventricular artery, so it is the muscle that ruptures after an inferior infarct.

parts.name: pulmonary_anterior_cusp
parts.description: The anterior cusp of the pulmonary valve, the most forward valve cusp in the heart.

parts.name: pulmonary_left_cusp
parts.description: The cusp on the patient's left side of the pulmonary valve.

parts.name: pulmonary_right_cusp
parts.description: The cusp on the patient's right side of the pulmonary valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_annulus
parts.description: The fibrous ring of the tricuspid orifice, about 3.6 cm across in this model. It stretches when the right ventricle dilates, causing functional tricuspid regurgitation.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_1
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_2
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_3
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_4
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_5
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_chorda_6
parts.description: Runs from the anterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_leaflet
parts.description: The largest leaflet, lying over the front wall of the right ventricle towards the outflow tract. Its chordae come from the anterior and septal papillary muscles.

parts.name: tricuspid_anterior_papillary_muscle
parts.description: The largest right ventricular papillary muscle, from the anterior wall; in life the moderator band (not modelled) joins it to the septum.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_1
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_2
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_3
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the posterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_4
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_5
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_chorda_6
parts.description: Runs from the posterior papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_leaflet
parts.description: The smallest leaflet, lying along the inferior wall of the ventricle. Its chordae come from the posterior and anterior papillary muscles.

parts.name: tricuspid_posterior_papillary_muscle
parts.description: Arises from the inferior wall of the right ventricle, often as two or three heads.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_1
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_2
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_3
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_4
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_5
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_chorda_6
parts.description: Runs from the septal papillary muscle to the anterior leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_leaflet
parts.description: Attached to the interventricular septum, with chordae from the septal and posterior papillary muscles. The atrioventricular node and bundle lie close to its base (the triangle of Koch), so surgery here risks heart block; in Ebstein anomaly it is displaced towards the apex.

parts.name: tricuspid_septal_papillary_muscle
parts.description: The smallest right ventricular papillary muscle, arising from the septum, sometimes rudimentary.

parts.name: Sinoatrial (SA) node
parts.description: Sinoatrial (SA) node: the pacemaker. In the lecture's words it lies medial to the opening of the superior vena cava, in the wall of the right atrium; here it is the crescent along the junction of the vena cava with the atrium, starting where the SA nodal artery ends. Its modified cardiac muscle cells generate action potentials spontaneously, about 70-80 a minute at rest, and each spreads through the atrial walls and on to the AV node. Gross anatomy texts put it at the top of the crista terminalis, just under the epicardium. Drawn thicker than life: it is 1-2 cm long but only a few millimetres thick.

parts.name: Anterior internodal pathway
parts.description: Anterior internodal pathway: runs from the SA node forward and down the front of the interatrial septum to the AV node, and gives off the Bachmann bundle to the left atrium. The lecture says these pathways conduct action potentials from the SA node to the AV node faster than the rest of the atrial muscle; the trip takes about 0.04 s. They are not insulated like the AV bundle: they are lines of well-aligned atrial muscle, and anatomists still argue whether they are separate tracts at all.

parts.name: Middle internodal pathway
parts.description: Middle internodal pathway (Wenckebach): runs from the SA node behind the superior vena cava and down the interatrial septum to the AV node. The lecture says these pathways conduct action potentials from the SA node to the AV node faster than the rest of the atrial muscle; the trip takes about 0.04 s. They are not insulated like the AV bundle: they are lines of well-aligned atrial muscle, and anatomists still argue whether they are separate tracts at all.

parts.name: Posterior internodal pathway
parts.description: Posterior internodal pathway (Thorel): runs from the SA node down the crista terminalis on the lateral wall, then along the ridge between the inferior vena cava and the coronary sinus opening to the back of the AV node. The lecture says these pathways conduct action potentials from the SA node to the AV node faster than the rest of the atrial muscle; the trip takes about 0.04 s. They are not insulated like the AV bundle: they are lines of well-aligned atrial muscle, and anatomists still argue whether they are separate tracts at all.

parts.name: Bachmann bundle (interatrial pathway)
parts.description: Bachmann bundle (interatrial pathway): a band of atrial muscle that carries the impulse from the right atrium across the roof of the atria to the left atrium, so both atria contract almost together. Like the internodal pathways it is a preferential route, not an insulated tract.

parts.name: Atrioventricular (AV) node
parts.description: Atrioventricular (AV) node: in the lecture's words, medial to the right AV (tricuspid) valve. It lies low on the right-atrial side of the septum, just above the attachment of the septal leaflet and in front of the opening of the coronary sinus (the triangle of Koch). Action potentials are conducted more slowly here than anywhere else in the system (small cells with few gap junctions and few myofibrils), giving a delay of about 0.1 s (0.11 s in the lecture) that lets the atria finish contracting before the ventricles start. The thinner tail toward the coronary sinus is its inferior extension. It is supplied by the AV nodal artery, usually from the right coronary artery, so an inferior infarct can cause heart block.

parts.name: Atrioventricular (AV) bundle (bundle of His)
parts.description: AV bundle (bundle of His): passes through a hole in the fibrous skeleton (the central fibrous body, here) to the interventricular septum. It is the only normal electrical connection between the atria and the ventricles, and conduction speeds up dramatically here after the slow AV node. It runs to the crest of the muscular septum just below the aortic valve and divides into the right and left bundle branches. Compression or ischaemia of the bundle is one cause of complete heart block.

parts.name: Central fibrous body
parts.description: Central fibrous body: the strongest part of the fibrous skeleton, dense connective tissue binding the mitral, tricuspid and aortic rings together. The skeleton insulates the atrial muscle from the ventricular muscle, so the only way through is the hole that carries the AV bundle, shown pierced here. Drawn as a simplified block between the two rings.

parts.name: Septomarginal trabecula (moderator band)
parts.description: Septomarginal trabecula (moderator band): a muscular bridge across the right ventricle from the septum to the base of the anterior papillary muscle. It carries much of the right bundle branch, a short cut that activates the papillary muscle early so the tricuspid chordae are tight before the ventricle ejects. It is not in the whole-heart model and was added here.

parts.name: Right bundle branch
parts.description: Right bundle branch: extends beneath the endocardium on the right side of the interventricular septum toward the apex of the right ventricle; much of it crosses in the moderator band to the anterior papillary muscle before breaking up into Purkinje fibres. If it is blocked, the right ventricle depolarizes late, through ordinary muscle, and the QRS complex widens.

parts.name: Left bundle branch
parts.description: Left bundle branch: leaves the AV bundle just below the aortic valve and extends beneath the endocardium on the left side of the septum toward the apex of the left ventricle. It is broader than the right branch and fans into an anterior and a posterior fascicle, with septal fibres (shown running toward the apex). A block widens the QRS complex.

parts.name: Left anterior fascicle
parts.description: Left anterior (superior) fascicle of the left bundle branch: crosses the front of the left ventricle toward the anterolateral papillary muscle. Long and thin, it is the fascicle most often blocked; a block swings the electrical axis to the left.

parts.name: Left posterior fascicle
parts.description: Left posterior (inferior) fascicle of the left bundle branch: shorter and broader, it runs to the posteromedial papillary muscle and the inferior wall.

parts.name: Purkinje fibres (left ventricle)
parts.description: Purkinje fibres (left ventricle): large-diameter cardiac muscle cells with few myofibrils and many gap junctions, forming the subendocardial network that conducts the action potential to the ventricular muscle cells. They are densest toward the apex and penetrate the myocardium, so the inner wall near the apex is stimulated first and contraction spreads from the apex toward the base, wringing blood up toward the great vessels. Drawn as a simplified net, thicker than life.

parts.name: Purkinje fibres (right ventricle)
parts.description: Purkinje fibres (right ventricle): the subendocardial network of the right ventricle, fed by the right bundle branch through the moderator band. Like the left network it is densest toward the apex, so the right ventricle also contracts from the apex up. Drawn as a simplified net, thicker than life.

parts.name: Fibrous pericardium
parts.description: Fibrous pericardium: the tough, fibrous outer layer of the pericardial sac. It prevents overdistention of the heart and acts as an anchor, holding the heart in place in the mediastinum: below it is fused to the central tendon of the diaphragm, above it blends with the walls of the great vessels. Cut away at the front here. Outside to inside: fibrous pericardium, parietal layer, pericardial cavity, visceral layer (epicardium), myocardium, endocardium.

parts.name: Parietal layer of serous pericardium
parts.description: Parietal layer of the serous pericardium: a thin, transparent layer of simple squamous epithelium lining the inside of the fibrous pericardium. At the roots of the great vessels it folds back to become the visceral layer, like a fist pushed into a balloon, so the two are one continuous membrane (both blue here). The pericardial cavity lies between them.

parts.name: Visceral layer of serous pericardium (epicardium)
parts.description: Visceral layer of the serous pericardium, also called the epicardium: simple squamous epithelium covering the surface of the heart and the roots of the great vessels. It is the smooth outer surface of the heart and the outermost layer of the heart wall; the coronary vessels and fat lie just beneath it. Cut away at the front to show the myocardium.

parts.name: Diaphragm (central tendon)
parts.description: Diaphragm, simplified to a plate: the fibrous pericardium is fused to its central tendon, which anchors the heart from below.

parts.name: Myocardium (wall block)
parts.description: Myocardium in the wall block: cardiac muscle, by far the thickest layer, responsible for contraction. Layer 5. Drawn 3x life size: in life the left ventricle's myocardium is about 1 cm thick.

parts.name: Endocardium (wall block)
parts.description: Endocardium in the wall block: the smooth inner surface of the heart chambers, endothelium (simple squamous) on a thin layer of connective tissue. Layer 6, against the blood. It also covers the valves, and a smooth lining matters because a rough one makes blood clot. Drawn thicker than life.

parts.name: Epicardial connective tissue and fat (wall block)
parts.description: Under the epicardium's epithelium: loose connective tissue and fat in which the coronary arteries and cardiac veins run. It counts as part of the epicardium.

parts.name: Visceral layer of serous pericardium (epicardium) (wall block)
parts.description: Visceral layer of the serous pericardium = epicardium, in the wall block: simple squamous epithelium on the heart's surface. Layer 4, and it belongs to both lists: the inner layer of the pericardium and the outer layer of the heart wall.

parts.name: Pericardial cavity with pericardial fluid (wall block)
parts.description: Pericardial cavity with pericardial fluid: the thin space between the parietal and visceral layers. The fluid lets the heart slide against the sac with very little friction as it beats. Layer 3. In life it is only a film (about 15-50 mL in all), so it is drawn far wider here.

parts.name: Parietal layer of serous pericardium (wall block)
parts.description: Parietal layer of the serous pericardium in the wall block: simple squamous epithelium lining the fibrous pericardium. Layer 2. Drawn much thicker than life.

parts.name: Fibrous pericardium (wall block)
parts.description: Fibrous pericardium in the magnified wall block: dense fibrous connective tissue, the outermost layer. Layer 1 of 6 from outside in. Outside to inside: fibrous pericardium, parietal layer, pericardial cavity, visceral layer (epicardium), myocardium, endocardium.

parts.name: Coronary artery branch (wall block)
parts.description: A branch of a coronary artery running in the epicardial fat.

parts.name: Cardiac vein (wall block)
parts.description: A cardiac vein running in the epicardial fat beside the artery.

parts.name: Trabeculae carneae (wall block)
parts.description: Trabeculae carneae: muscular ridges and columns on the inside walls of the ventricles ("little beams of flesh"); a few are free bridges. They are myocardium covered by endocardium. (Pectinate muscles are the comb-like ridges of the auricles and right atrial wall.)

parts.name: Purkinje fibres (wall block)
parts.description: Purkinje fibres in the subendocardial layer, just beneath the endothelium (drawn on the surface so they can be seen): the fast-conducting cells that carry the impulse to the ventricular muscle.

parts.name: Right atrial wall (atrial block)
parts.description: Right atrial wall in the atrial block, 3x life size: thin atrial myocardium, about 2 mm in life, compared with about 10 mm in the left ventricle.

parts.name: Endocardium (atrial block)
parts.description: Endocardium lining the right atrium: smooth endothelium on a thin connective-tissue layer.

parts.name: Epicardium (atrial block)
parts.description: Epicardium (visceral pericardium) on the outer surface of the atrial wall.

parts.name: Crista terminalis (atrial block)
parts.description: Crista terminalis: the vertical muscular ridge inside the right atrium. The pectinate muscles run off it toward the auricle; behind it the wall is smooth (the sinus venarum, where the venae cavae enter). The SA node lies at its upper end.

parts.name: Pectinate muscles (atrial block)
parts.description: Pectinate muscles: muscular ridges in the auricles and the right atrial wall, lined up like the teeth of a comb ("pectinate" = comb-like). Compare the irregular net of trabeculae carneae in the ventricular block below.
